mechanics.premise: A king charged with retrieving a reanimated corpse hears, night after night, a story from it — each ending in a question he must answer correctly or lose it again: a riddle-cycle across twenty-five attempts (frame verified).
mechanics.deflation_targets: Royal omniscience itself — the sovereign is repeatedly outwitted and corrected by a creature that should be beneath him (frame-level inference; individual tales not inspected).
mechanics.licensed_frame: The riddle-game's explicit rules license the corpse's impertinence toward the king: mockery is permitted because the frame defines when it must stop — the purest structural example of bounded license in this silo.
mechanics.point_of_view: Nested frame narration: outer pursuit, inner tales told by the corpse, closing riddle addressed to the king.
mechanics.style_and_devices: Story-within-story with a compulsory final question; comic irony of the dead instructing the living sovereign (described from the verified frame only).
mechanics.dialogue: The corpse's taunting questions against the king's duty-bound answers carry the status reversal.
mechanics.emotional_progression: Serial suspense (will he answer?) punctuated by the pleasure of watching authority be tested and found talkable-to.
mechanics.boundaries_and_restraint: Analysis deliberately partial: only the frame and bibliographic identity were verified, so mechanics claims stay at frame level and no tale's content or morals are asserted.
mechanics.conventions: Vetala/Betaal riddle-cycle, circulating across Indian language traditions (the uniform title itself evidences the Hindi recension).
mechanics.innovation_or_subversion: Encodes licensed irreverence toward sovereignty as a formal rule of the game — impertinence with an expiry built into the plot.
mechanics.critical_reception: Known in English chiefly through Burton's 1870 rendering; source recension behind his translation unverified this session.
mechanics.audience_reception: The cycle remains widely known across South Asian popular culture; reception of Burton's specific English version not examined.
